name: com.orbb.mcp/research
title: Orbb Research
description: Who knows whom and how well: find who could introduce you, from the public professional record.

tools.name: orbbai_capabilities
tools.description:
What Orbb can and cannot answer. Called bare it returns a short overview and the list of questions it settles, with how much of each is public record and how much needs data only you hold.

The longer parts are named in that overview and fetched by name: the kinds of research and their limits, and what makes an introduction land.

Free.

about.description: Omitted, it returns the overview, which names the other parts (`overview` asks for it by name). `kinds` — the kinds of research, each population, limits and depths. `asking` — what makes an introduction land, and which half is yours. `questions` — what Orbb answers and what needs your data. `all` — every part at once, and long.

tools.name: orbbai_people_resolve
tools.description:
Turns names into the handles Orbb takes, for a question about particular people rather than a company. The handles go to `orbbai_plan`.

IT RETURNS CANDIDATES AND NEVER PICKS: a common name comes back as several people with a headline and a company each, and the choice between them is yours.

Free.

names.description: A full name, an email, or a LinkedIn URL. Add a company or title to the string where you have one — "Dana Mor, Head of Data at Acme" resolves far more often.

ask.description: What this is for, in your user's own words. Optional; it is what later calls in this session weigh an answer against.

tools.name: orbbai_plan
tools.description:
The way in to somebody new: who could introduce you to a person or to someone at a company, and what it would take to find out — a price in Research Tokens, a time, and a `planId`. Nothing starts here except the free roster pass of a company; `orbbai_run_start` takes the `planId`.

Asked as: who could introduce me to them · who is best placed to make the introduction · what is the warmest path in · how do I get a warm introduction at this company · who do we already know there · how well do they know each other.

And asked as: find me everybody who · build me a list of · who are the <role> at · which people match these conditions · find <role> in <place>. Nobody has to be named first: `titles` with a `country` or `cities` searches the whole public index and comes back with a column per condition and a yes, no or not-checked in every cell.

The routes are read off the public professional record. Anyone named through `orbbai_ours_remember` is crossed in and ranks first.

WHAT IS GIVEN DECIDES THE KIND, and all four take the goal in `ask`:

- a `company`, for "who inside this company could we reach", scoped by `inside` — comes back with a shortlist of the people there worth going through, and a `runId` for `orbbai_run_status`.

- `handles` from `orbbai_people_resolve` or `orbbai_table_read`, for particular people already named.

- `titles` with a `country` or `cities`, to find people nobody has named yet.

- `reachFrom`, for a chain, whatever else is given but a `recipe`: somebody out of reach, walked to from your own side.

A refusal names the one missing field.

Free, every kind: a `company` starts a free roster pass; `orbbai_run_start` and `orbbai_run_continue` spend.

ask.description: What your user wants, in their own words — a sentence, not a filter. Orbb plans from it. Optional, and every answer in this session is weaker without it.

handles.description: Handles from `orbbai_people_resolve` or `orbbai_table_read`. Plans a person run.

company.description: One company, by name or domain, for "who inside this company" when you have no names yet.

inside.description: WHO INSIDE THAT COMPANY, in your user’s own words and a FEW WORDS LONG — "their CFO", "finance leadership", "the revenue org". Several functions go in comma-separated and each one named gets its best person before any gets a second. Required with `company`; if your user has not said, ask them rather than guess. IT IS NOT THE GOAL: `ask` says what the research is FOR and this says who it is ABOUT, and a sentence here scopes the roster on prose.

seniority.description: The lowest seniority worth reaching. Required with `company`, together with `ask` and `inside`: the run cannot stop and ask for them later. Also used for `handles`; a search ignores it.

reachFrom.description: PLANS A CHAIN: who on your own side to start from, by handle. `handles` become who to reach. A chain walks up to three hops and returns EVERY route it finds, scored on its weakest hop. Not the first answer to "how do I reach X" — research the target first, and reach for this when their own circle comes back thin.

titles.description: Roles to search for, e.g. ["VP Data", "Head of Analytics"]. Plans a search.

finds.description: SEARCH ONLY. Conditions about their EMPLOYER, one per thing your user said, in their own words — ["raised a funding round", "sells to enterprise"]. Each becomes a column with a yes / no / not-checked verdict per row, so the answer shows which part of the question each person meets.

personFinds.description: SEARCH ONLY. Conditions about the PERSON that are not their job title — ["worked at a competitor before", "posts about outbound"]. The dividing line is whose property it is: an employer condition goes in `finds`, where it is checked once per company and shared.

optional.description: WHICH OF THOSE CONDITIONS SHOULD RANK RATHER THAN GATE, copied EXACTLY from `finds` or `personFinds`. Anything not named here HAS TO HOLD. MEASURED: a search whose every condition gated found 3,500 people by role and returned NONE. What your user LEADS with is the requirement; "ideally", "bonus if", "preferably" mark a wish — and where their sentence does not say, ask rather than guessing.

country.description: THE TWO-LETTER ISO CODE: DE, GB, IL. A name matches nothing. A search saying nowhere is refused: it would match everybody and come back with whoever happens to rank first.

companies.description: Domains or names, where the search is about particular companies.

depth.description: Leave out unless your user asked. Absent means Orbb chooses; nothing forces Deep.

recipe.description: A whole playbook by its recipe id, e.g. `account-plan`, `multithread`, `person-brief`, `referral-campaign`, where recipes are switched on; an unknown id is refused with the known ones. Beside it send only `ask` and `inputs`: any other field is refused, so its company, depth (`standard` or `deep`), inside or seniority go in `inputs`. A free recipe answers at once; a priced one comes back with a `planId` for `orbbai_run_start`.

inputs.description: What the recipe runs on, by its snake_case input name, e.g. `company`, `person`, `engaged`, `customers`, `company_run`. Your user's own side — who is engaged, their customers, their accounts — goes here; Orbb never infers it. Read only with `recipe`; a missing, unknown or wrongly shaped input is refused with the input named.

tools.name: orbbai_run_start
tools.description:
Agrees to a plan and starts it. The plan it names carries the price, and this is the call that spends against the balance of whoever owns the connection.

It takes the plan id and nothing else, so what runs is what was quoted. A different set of people is a different plan, at a new price.

Runs take minutes; `orbbai_run_status` reports progress.

Spends Research Tokens.

planId.description: The `planId` from `orbbai_plan`. The only thing this takes.

tools.name: orbbai_run_status
tools.description:
Where a run is and what it has found so far. Runs take minutes, so it reports progress rather than a final answer until it has one.

A run can pause and ask: it reports what finishing would buy and cost, and goes no further until you agree. When it ends, `orbbai_read_report` hands back a person’s findings and `orbbai_table_read` the table a search leaves; `orbbai_ways_in_for_a_goal` weighs finished research against a goal.

Free.

runId.description: The run id from `orbbai_run_start`, or from `orbbai_plan` with a `company`, which starts its run while planning.

tools.name: orbbai_run_continue
tools.description:
Agrees to the judged half of a run that stopped to show its price. The first press measured a shortlist for free; this one buys the research on it, and answers with the run that now carries on, which `orbbai_run_status` follows.

A company run stops once it knows who is at the company and what researching them would cost. That measurement is the only honest basis for agreeing, which is why there are two presses and not one. YOUR READER DECIDES WHO IS ON THE LIST: show them what `orbbai_run_status` reported and send back the handles they kept. Agreeing without showing them spends their money on a list they never saw.

Asked as: yes, go ahead · research those people · drop the last two and run the rest.

Spends Research Tokens against the balance of whoever owns the connection.

people.description: The `handle` of each person your reader kept, exactly as `orbbai_run_status` lists them. A reader can add people as well as take them off: any handle the shortlist offered — chosen, worth a look or named on the web — can be agreed to. The list you send replaces the shortlist, so to add somebody send the chosen handles they keep plus theirs. Anybody else is refused here — plan a person run with their `handles` instead. Leave it out to agree to the shortlist as proposed: a reader who changed nothing has still agreed. A reader who kept nobody needs no call at all: nothing is spent until this one.

tools.name: orbbai_run_stop
tools.description:
Stops a run and keeps what it found: the rows already in it stay readable. There is no refund for what was spent, and it is harmless on a run that has already finished.

Free.

tools.name: orbbai_who_knows_them
tools.description:
One person in; the people around them out — each with how strongly they know them and the evidence underneath: who they worked alongside and for how long, who they interact with publicly, and where each of those people is now. One call, a few seconds, nothing to poll.

Asked as: who could introduce me to them · does anyone know them · who is best placed to make the introduction · how well do they know each other · who has influence with them · whose opinion do they listen to · is there a mutual connection · what is the warmest path in.

And asked as, when there is no time: before a call · I am about to meet them · quick sense of who they know · who should I know about before this meeting · I see them next week.

And asked as, when getting it wrong is expensive: this is our biggest deal · I need to be right about this · who genuinely knows them · who knows them well enough to introduce me.

IT PINS THE PERSON ITSELF, so one call is enough. A LinkedIn URL or the public id after /in/ is read directly; a full name is resolved on the open record, and the answer says how sure it was and hands back the profile to confirm. A single word is read as a public id, so send a full name.

Reading every one of those people, scoring each tie against your goal and ranking them is a run, `orbbai_plan`. This one cannot rank.

Send `about` when the question says what the introduction is for, and `userIs` with `userWorksAt` when you know them: the answer then marks who your own user has worked alongside, and who sits at your user’s company now or used to. Without them it cannot say whether your user knows any of these people.

Free.

person.description: Who to look at: a LinkedIn profile URL, the public id after `/in/`, or their full name. A URL or a public id is read directly; a name is pinned first and is a judgement. A SINGLE WORD IS READ AS A PUBLIC ID, never as a name — for somebody known only as 'Dana', send the full name.

company.description: Where they work. WHAT PINS A COMMON NAME — a name on its own is several people and this is the field that decides which. Ignored when `person` is a URL or a public id.

email.description: Their work email, if you have one. Read only when `company` is not sent, and ignored when `person` is a URL or a public id.

about.description: WHAT YOU WANT THE INTRODUCTION FOR, if the question says — a department, a kind of role, or a seniority ('revenue', 'engineering', 'the exec team', 'anyone senior'). It ranks and filters the people around them by what each of them does now and did then. Where nobody around them fits, the answer says so and still shows what is held.

userIs.description: WHO YOUR OWN USER IS — their LinkedIn profile URL (anything else is not read), not the person you are asking about. THE STRONGEST FIELD HERE: with it the answer says which of these people your user has worked alongside THEMSELVES, where, for how long and how strongly — a path that needs no introduction rather than one that does.

userWorksAt.description: WHERE YOUR OWN USER WORKS — their employer, not the person you are asking about. Send it and the answer marks anybody already reachable from your user's own side: somebody who worked alongside them and now sits at your user's company, or used to. It is the one field that turns a list of names into 'these two are already yours'. One string, a company name or domain.

tools.name: orbbai_who_knows_someone_there
tools.description:
One company in; ways in out — each a named person who left that company and a named person still inside whose time there overlapped theirs, with how many months they were there together. The person who left is the one you can approach. One call, the public record only, nothing to poll.

Asked as: who do we know at X · has anyone got a line into X · I'm cold on X, is there anyone we can use · who could introduce us to someone senior at X · is there a warm path into X · does anybody know anyone there · who can get us in · who used to work there.

And asked as, when getting it wrong is expensive: this is our biggest deal · board meeting Monday · we have been trying to get into X for a year · I need the strongest path in · nothing has worked so far.

IT READS PART OF THE ROSTER AND CANNOT RANK. Everyone there, cut to who matters, then each of them researched and ranked, is a run: `orbbai_plan`. Who is worth talking to at a company already researched, and who this workspace reaches inside, is `orbbai_held`.

Send `inCity` when the question names a place, and `userIs` with `userWorksAt` when you know them: the answer then marks which of these people are already reachable from your own side. Without them it cannot say whether your user knows any of them, because that half is not in the public record.

Free.

company.description: The company to get into: a domain (snowflake.com), its name, or its LinkedIn id `company/<slug>`. A name usually finds it and is a guess — the answer says which company it read. A LinkedIn company URL is not read: send its `company/<slug>` id.

about.description: The part of the company that matters, if any — a department or a kind of role ('engineering', 'sales', 'data', 'security'). It ranks and filters the people found inside. Where nobody inside fits, the answer says so and still shows what is held.

inCity.description: WHERE THEY SHOULD BE, if the question says — a city, a state or a country ('NYC', 'New York', 'London', 'Israel'). A CITY IS NOT A DEPARTMENT, which is why it is a field of its own; send both when the question has both. Somebody whose record names no place is not excluded — "we do not know where they are" is not "they are somewhere else".

userIs.description: WHO YOUR OWN USER IS — their LinkedIn profile URL (anything else is not read), not the company you are asking about. THE STRONGEST FIELD HERE: with it the answer says which of these people your user has worked alongside THEMSELVES, where, for how long and how strongly — a path that needs no introduction rather than one that does.

userWorksAt.description: WHERE YOUR OWN USER WORKS — their employer, not the company you are asking about. Send it and the answer marks anybody already reachable from your user's own side: somebody who left this company and now sits at your user's company, or used to. It is the one field that turns a list of names into 'these two are already yours'. One string, a company name or domain.

tools.name: orbbai_playbooks
tools.description:
A library of worked workflows: scoring accounts by who you can reach, finding the route into every open opportunity, spotting deals with no relationship behind them, prioritising outbound by warm access, finding the missing executive sponsor, picking an event invite list. Each one says what it does, when it runs, the steps, the calls it makes and what your own systems supply.

Asked as: what could we build with this · what should we automate · how would I wire this into our own systems · what do other teams do with this · we want to prioritise outbound by warm access, how · is there a repeatable version of this · how do I set this up for the team · what is the best way to use this.

TWO WAYS TO USE AN ANSWER, and the playbook gives both: run it once now over whatever is in front of your user, or take the build spec for the recurring version — the trigger, the steps and the calls, written to be set up in their own automation, because nothing here subscribes to anything.

Send `about` with what your user is trying to do for the two or three that fit, or `slug` for one in full.

Free.

about.description: WHAT THEY ARE TRYING TO DO, in their own words — "prioritise outbound", "we keep losing deals we have no relationship into", "warm intros for recruiting". Matched against the library by team, by job, by what it needs connected and by the words themselves. Omitted, it returns the shortest overview of what is there.

slug.description: One playbook, in full: what it does, when it runs, the steps to build it, which calls it makes, what their own systems must supply, and a worked example. Send it after a match looks right.

tools.name: orbbai_held
tools.description:
What this workspace has already researched, by kind, with the date each piece was written and how old it is. A held answer is immediate; researching the same subject again spends Research Tokens to learn nothing new.

Asked as: what do we already have on them · have we looked at this person before · what changed since we last looked · what have we run on this company.

Free.

ask.description: What this is for, in your user's own words. It does not filter what comes back — `about` does that. It is recorded in this session, and later calls weigh their answers against it.

about.description: Limit to one kind of research. `person` is one circle, `people` a goal read across one or more people’s circles, `chain` a route to somebody out of reach, `company` a roster and `company-intent` one read for a goal. Out means everything held.

tools.name: orbbai_read_report
tools.description:
A finished report in full: the people it found, the reasoning behind each one, and what the run could not establish. Where `orbbai_held` says what is held, this is how to read it.

Asked as: what did we find on them · open that report · who was in their circle · what did the run say about them · read me what we have.

A report is found by what its subject is called, so the name you were given is enough. IT IS ALREADY PAID FOR, and researching the same subject again spends Research Tokens to learn nothing new.

Free.

report.description: The report id from `orbbai_held`, a person’s handle, OR THE PERSON’S NAME — a report is found by what it says its subject is called, so the name you were given is enough.

people.description: How many people to read from each list, up to 40. Leave it out for a dozen.

ask.description: What you are looking for, in your user's own words.

tools.name: orbbai_ways_in_for_a_goal
tools.description:
Routes out of research already finished, ranked against the goal you give it, with the reasoning under each and two warnings about how to read them.

Asked as: what do I actually do now · who should I approach first · what is the first move · rank these against what I am trying to do. Where `orbbai_held` says what is held, this reads it and says what to do with it.

It reads only what this workspace already holds and researches nobody: on a person or company nothing has been run on, it has nothing to rank and says so — `orbbai_plan` is what goes and finds out.

One person’s run that has just finished is a report rather than this: `orbbai_read_report` hands back the closest ties it examined, strongest first (a dozen by default, more on request), with how strong each tie is, how much weight they carry, a confidence beside both, and what a deep run decided to do.

THIS IS FOR ONE GOAL WEIGHED ACROSS THE PEOPLE OR COMPANIES YOU NAME whose research is done — several circles at once, and who more than one of them reaches.

Free.

subjects.description: Who or what the routes should lead to. Handles or companies already researched.

ask.description: REQUIRED HERE, unlike elsewhere. What your user is trying to achieve, in their own words. Without it there is nothing to rank routes against, so this refuses.

tools.name: orbbai_table_read
tools.description:
The rows themselves, out of a table this workspace already built: every person with their title, their employer, the verdict on each condition that was asked of them, and their LinkedIn handle in square brackets after the name.

Asked as: who is on the list · show me the names · who at <company> came back · how many answered <condition> · which rows were never checked · what did the search actually find.

THE HANDLES ARE WHY THE NEXT CALL IS FREE: everybody in a table is already resolved, so they go straight to `orbbai_plan`, up to 40 per plan.

A page at a time, and the counts are over every row (every row at `company` when one is given), not the page. Use `at` to walk it.

It reads what is there and researches nobody, so a row no condition was put to reads not asked rather than no — narrowing is what asks a new one, and that costs.

Free.

table.description: The table to read, by the id a run or a narrowing gave you.

at.description: Zero-based: the first row is 0. Each page names the `at` for the next one, in the table’s own order.

company.description: Only rows whose employer, as the table shows it, contains this text (any case) — a short name can catch other employers. Omit for every row.

tools.name: orbbai_table_narrow
tools.description:
A new table from one already built, keeping the rows that meet conditions you write as sentences. The original is untouched.

Each condition is judged once per row, and every condition in one call is judged in one pass.

Costs a judgement per row.

table.description: The table to narrow, by the id a run or a reading gave you.

keep.description: Conditions to keep, as plain sentences — "has changed job in the last year". Orbb judges each row against them.

called.description: A name for the new table. Optional.

tools.name: orbbai_ours_remember
tools.description:
Records who is on your own side — colleagues, advisors, investors, customers, former teammates. Orbb maps the public record, and who you can reach through is the half only you hold: every later answer is better for having it.

The names in a CRM, an inbox, a calendar or call recordings belong here. It adds and never removes, and one call carries up to a hundred people.

Free.

kind.description: YOUR USER'S OWN WORD FOR IT, not the nearest one of ours — "design partner", "former colleague", "board member". The vocabulary is open on purpose.

company.description: Where they are now, if you know.

linkedin.description: Their LinkedIn URL. Best for pinning them down.

note.description: Anything that changes how the relationship should be used: who owns it, how warm, when it was last live, what not to ask for.

people.description: The people on your user's own side of the table.
